newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Netanyahu condemns pig posters in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu condemns pig posters in Hebron.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called the Arab mayor of Hebron on Sunday to condemn the distribution there of posters depicting the Moslem Prophet Mohammad as a pig stomping on the Koran.
Israeli police said on Saturday they had arrested a 25-year-old Jewish woman from Jerusalem suspected of pasting the posters on 20 storefronts near a Jewish settlement enclave in the West Bank.

"This runs counter to our outlook as Jews and our respect and appreciation for the Islamic religion and for its founder the Prophet Mohammad," Netanyahu said in a statement after speaking to Palestinian mayor Mustafa al-Natsheh by phone.
Dozens of protesters took to the streets in Hebron on Saturday after Palestinian shopkeepers discovered the posters. Islam and Judaism view pigs as unclean and ban the eating of pork.
"We arrested her after she threw a rock through the windshield of an Arab car in Hebron. Ten posters were found in her possession. She wanted to stir up trouble," a police spokesman said.

Israel handed over most of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule in January but kept troops in about 20 percent of the city to guard some 400 Jewish settlers who live and study in fortified enclaves in the heart of the city of 100,000 Palestinians.
The town has been the scene of clashes between Palestinians and Israeli troops since Israel's groundbreaking in March on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem plunged peacemaking into crisis.
